result_text:
I checked all three superseded ADRs against every ADR and RFC record. Only four accepted records count as header citations: ADR-0031, ADR-0032 and ADR-0034 (ADRs) and RFC-0042, all citing ADR-0023. RFC-0050 cites it too, but its own header says ADR-0023 is being superseded (see the second reading point). ADR-0050 and ADR-0125 have no header citations under the Term. I read every header myself, and every other match the search found is in a record body.

```json
{"superseded": [
  {"id": "ADR-0023", "successors": ["ADR-0042"]},
  {"id": "ADR-0050", "successors": ["ADR-0109"]},
  {"id": "ADR-0125", "successors": ["ADR-0144"]}
 ],
 "citations": [
  {"superseded": "ADR-0023", "successors": ["ADR-0042"], "cited_by": "ADR-0031", "field": "Related"},
  {"superseded": "ADR-0023", "successors": ["ADR-0042"], "cited_by": "ADR-0032", "field": "Related"},
  {"superseded": "ADR-0023", "successors": ["ADR-0042"], "cited_by": "ADR-0034", "field": "Related"},
  {"superseded": "ADR-0023", "successors": ["ADR-0042"], "cited_by": "RFC-0042", "field": "Related"},
  {"superseded": "ADR-0023", "successors": ["ADR-0042"], "cited_by": "RFC-0050", "field": "Related"}
 ],
 "excluded": [
  {"superseded": "ADR-0023", "record": "ADR-0042", "why": "successor"},
  {"superseded": "ADR-0023", "record": "RFC-0051", "why": "names-successor"},
  {"superseded": "ADR-0050", "record": "ADR-0109", "why": "successor"},
  {"superseded": "ADR-0125", "record": "ADR-0144", "why": "successor"},
  {"superseded": "ADR-0125", "record": "ADR-0061", "why": "names-successor"}
 ],
 "reading_disagreements": [
  "ADR-0061 names ADR-0125 in its 'Superseded in part' field ('ADR-0125 D3,D4; ADR-0144 D1,D2,D8'). The Supersedes-field exclusion covers only 'Supersedes' and 'Supersedes in part', so that rule would not exclude this match. It is excluded anyway because the same header names the successor ADR-0144. A reading that also excluded the 'Superseded in part' field would give the same result.",
  "RFC-0050's Related field cites ADR-0023 and says it 'is superseded in this session'. It does not name ADR-0042, so under the Term as written it is a header citation, even though the record itself acknowledges the supersession. Someone checking intent rather than the literal Term might argue to exclude it."
 ]}
```

- **Which records count:** I took the set of records from the file-pattern definition in `rules.md`, checked against `listing.tsv`. I couldn't use the script's own admission logic, because I was only allowed to read `rules.md`, `listing.tsv` and the two record folders. I found the status words by searching for `- **Status:** <word>` and read the three superseded ADRs' headers in full. In ADR files, that status line was the only format I searched for.
- **Excluded list:** Successors appear only as `successor`, though each also carries its match in its `Supersedes` field. Several RFCs (0032, 0048, 0061, 0102) and ADRs (0035, 0043, 0112) mention these ADRs only below their first `## ` heading, so they aren't listed. ADR-0043's header names ADR-0042 but never ADR-0023.
- **Ambiguities in the Terms:**
  - "Match … as a whole word" doesn't say whether `ADR-0023's` counts. I treated the apostrophe as a word boundary, but no result here depends on it.
  - The Term doesn't say whether several matches in one record are one citation or many. I counted one per record and field.
  - The Supersedes-field exclusion leaves the mirror field (`Superseded in part`) open, as described in the first reading point.
